findings.reason: without naming a keep-if-word guard or seeding a non-self-mapping word (e.g. `landed`) the done-when cannot show the guard fires, so the section's own measure misses the defect it exists to prevent.
findings.text: the deliverable requires "keeping a state that is already one of the seven words", but the only raw-state→pane-word mapper, `_display_state` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:921), is not idempotent: its `PANE_STATES` frozensets for `halted`, `delivered`, `landed` and `dropped` do not contain their own names, so `_display_state("landed")`, `("delivered")`, `("halted")` and `("dropped")` all return "" (a blank left word), while it does keep `queued`/`working`/`waiting`. Test 1 checks only `working`, and test 2 seeds the VALUES of `PANE_STATES` (raw producer states such as `completed_unpromoted`), which never equal those four words, so a node that maps the seed with bare `_display_state` — the obvious reuse of §5's own mapper — passes both tests and the negative control while violating the deliverable for four of the seven words.

findings.reason: §5 is already declared `done`, so no dispatch can be mis-ordered today; the missing edge is bookkeeping that only matters if §5 is reopened while §6 builds.
findings.text: §6 exists to map remembered states to §5's pane words and reads `PANE_STATES`, which §5 owns, yet `plan-section-depends-on` names no dependency for s6, unlike §3→§5 and §5→§2 which declare exactly this kind of ordering for a shared table and file.

findings.reason: the deliverable's operative instruction ("where it takes the memory in") and the done-when scope the work to memory-seeded rows, so the node's implementation is unaffected even though the universal claim is false.
findings.text: the deliverable concludes "...so every left word a row draws is one of the seven", but the shipped renderer draws `new` as the left word on a run's first row (reckon/crew/ticker.py:2054), and §5's own done-when asserts a first row "starts with `new`" — a word outside the seven — so the section's closing claim is falsified by the code and the plan it summarises.
